chunks: 1628 - Zakat may be permissible for the owner of seven hundred, while it is forbidden for the owner of fifty, if the owner of seven hundred has many dependents such that, were he to divide it among them, it would not suffice him. So let him keep himself restrained from it for himself, and let him take it for his dependents. As for the owner of fifty, it is forbidden for him if he is alone and is a craftsman working with it, and through it he earns what suffices him, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

key_terms.الزَّكَاةُ: zakat, the alms-tax being discussed as lawful or unlawful to receive
key_terms.صَاحِبِ السَّبْعِمِائَةِ: the one possessing seven hundred, used here as an example of someone who may still qualify due to need
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْخَمْسِينَ: the one possessing fifty, used here as an example of someone who may be ineligible despite lower holdings
key_terms.عِيَالٌ: dependents or family members whose maintenance affects financial sufficiency
key_terms.مُحْتَرِفٌ: a person with a trade or profession
key_terms.يَكْفِيهِ: suffices him; meets his essential needs

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible for someone who owns property or capital to receive zakat?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal distinction in zakat eligibility based not merely on nominal wealth, but on actual sufficiency and dependents. A person with greater assets may still lawfully receive zakat if his many dependents make his wealth insufficient, while one with less may be barred if his trade adequately supports him.
